instruction: Stream the logs of the api deployment in the staging namespace, including the previous container if it crashed.
context: kubectl: -f follows the stream, --tail limits the initial backlog, and deploy/api resolves to one pod of the deployment. Use -p instead of -f to read the previous container after a crash loop. kubectl ships no man page; kubectl logs --help is the reference.

instruction: List all pods in every namespace showing which node each one runs on.
context: kubectl: -A is shorthand for --all-namespaces and cannot be combined with -n. -o wide adds the node and pod IP columns that the default table omits.

instruction: Print just the container image used by each pod in the default namespace.
context: kubectl: -o jsonpath evaluates a JSONPath template against the response. The range and end pair iterates items, and escape sequences must be quoted so the shell does not eat the backslashes.

instruction: Find out why a pod is stuck in Pending.
context: kubectl: describe renders the object plus its recent Events, and the Events block is where scheduling failures such as insufficient CPU or unbound volume claims are explained. get -o yaml shows spec and status but omits events.

instruction: Open an interactive shell inside a running pod.
context: kubectl: -i keeps stdin open and -t allocates a TTY. The bare -- separates kubectl's own flags from the command run inside the container; without it, flags after the pod name are parsed by kubectl.

instruction: Reach a cluster service from my laptop on local port 8080.
context: kubectl: port-forward maps LOCAL:REMOTE, so 8080:80 exposes the service's port 80 locally as 8080. Targeting svc/ load-balances across pods, while targeting pod/ pins to one instance.

instruction: Check which cluster my kubectl commands are currently pointed at.
context: kubectl: config current-context prints the active context name from the kubeconfig. Running this before any destructive command is the standard guard against acting on production by accident.

instruction: Wait until a deployment has finished rolling out.
context: kubectl: rollout status blocks until the rollout completes and exits non-zero on failure or timeout, which makes it usable as a deployment gate in CI. --timeout accepts Go duration strings such as 90s or 5m.

instruction: Roll a bad deployment back to the previous revision.
context: kubectl: rollout undo reverts to the prior revision recorded in the deployment history. Add --to-revision=N to target a specific one, which rollout history lists.

instruction: Run one specific test in the syntax crate and show its printed output.
context: cargo: -p selects one workspace package and --test names an integration test target under tests/. Arguments after the bare -- are passed to the test harness, where --nocapture stops it from swallowing stdout.

instruction: Type-check the whole workspace quickly without producing binaries.
context: cargo: check runs the compiler front end and skips code generation, so it is several times faster than build. --all-targets extends the check to tests, benches, and examples, which plain check omits.

instruction: Run the linter across the workspace and fail the build on any warning.
context: cargo: arguments after -- go to rustc, so -D warnings promotes every lint to a hard error. This is the standard CI invocation because clippy otherwise exits zero with warnings printed.

instruction: Add serde to this crate with derive support enabled.
context: cargo: add edits Cargo.toml and resolves a compatible version. --features enables optional features at the same time; --no-default-features is separate and is often needed alongside it.

instruction: Find out why two versions of the same crate are being compiled.
context: cargo: tree -d lists only packages present at more than one version and shows which dependents pull each one. -i inverts the tree to show what depends on a given crate.

instruction: Run one specific binary target in release mode with an argument.
context: cargo: --bin picks a named binary when a package has several, and --release enables optimizations. Everything after -- is forwarded to the program rather than parsed by cargo.

instruction: Run the project's test suite in its managed virtual environment.
context: uv: run resolves and syncs the project environment before executing, so no manual activation is needed. It reads pyproject.toml and uv.lock from the nearest project root. uv has no man page; uv help run is the reference.

instruction: Install this project's dependencies including the development group.
context: uv: sync makes the environment exactly match uv.lock, removing anything extra. --dev includes the dev dependency group. Unlike pip install, sync is subtractive as well as additive.

instruction: Add pytest as a development dependency of this project.
context: uv: add writes the requirement into pyproject.toml, updates uv.lock, and installs it. --dev places it in the dev group rather than the runtime dependencies.

instruction: Pin this project to Python 3.14 and install that interpreter if needed.
context: uv: python pin writes .python-version, and uv fetches a managed interpreter automatically when one is missing. uv python install downloads without pinning.

instruction: Run ruff once without installing it into the project.
context: uv: uvx is the alias for uv tool run and executes a tool in a throwaway isolated environment, leaving the project untouched. uv tool install makes it permanent instead.

instruction: Lint the project and automatically apply the safe fixes.
context: ruff: check lints and --fix applies only fixes marked safe. --unsafe-fixes opts into the rest, and --diff previews changes without writing them. ruff check and ruff format are separate subcommands.

instruction: Verify formatting in CI without rewriting any files.
context: ruff: format --check exits non-zero when a file would be reformatted and changes nothing on disk, which is the CI-safe mode. --diff additionally prints what would change.

instruction: Check only for unused imports across the training directory.
context: ruff: --select restricts the run to specific rule codes, where F401 is the unused-import rule inherited from Pyflakes. --ignore removes rules from the configured set instead.

instruction: See what tasks this project's justfile defines.
context: just: --list prints every recipe with its documentation comment. Recipes starting with an underscore are hidden. just has no man page; --help and the justfile itself are the reference.

instruction: Run the deploy recipe passing staging as its argument.
context: just: positional words after the recipe name bind to the recipe's declared parameters in order. Unlike make, just recipes are not file targets and always run when invoked.

instruction: Start a throwaway Ubuntu shell with the current directory mounted.
context: docker: --rm deletes the container on exit, -it gives an interactive TTY, -v bind-mounts host:container, and -w sets the working directory inside. $PWD must be quoted so paths containing spaces survive.

instruction: Follow the last hundred log lines of a running container.
context: docker: -f follows the stream and --tail limits the backlog. --since accepts a timestamp or a relative duration such as 10m for narrowing an incident window.

instruction: Get a shell inside an already running container.
context: docker: exec runs an additional process in an existing container, unlike run which creates a new one. -it is required for an interactive shell or the session exits immediately.

instruction: Reclaim disk space from stopped containers and dangling images without being prompted.
context: docker: system prune removes stopped containers, unused networks, and dangling images. -f skips the confirmation. Adding -a also deletes every unused image, not just untagged ones, which is far more destructive.

instruction: List the containers that exited with a non-zero status.
context: docker: -a includes stopped containers, which the default listing hides. Repeated --filter expressions are combined, and the exited= filter matches on the container's exit code.

instruction: Open a pull request against main with a title and body from the command line.
response: gh pr create --base main --title 'Add curated corpus' --body 'Adds first-party training rows.'
context: gh: pr create infers the head branch from the current checkout and --base names the target. Supplying both --title and --body skips the interactive editor, which is what makes it scriptable.

instruction: Watch the CI checks on the current pull request until they finish.
context: gh: pr checks reports each check run's status and exits non-zero if any failed. --watch polls until completion, making it usable as a blocking gate before merging.

instruction: Show the failing log output from the most recent workflow run.
context: gh: run view without an ID targets the most recent run. --log-failed prints only the steps that failed, which is far shorter than --log for a large matrix build.

instruction: List the names of the twenty most recently updated repositories in an organization.
context: gh: api performs an authenticated REST call and --jq applies a jq filter to the response without needing jq installed. The URL must be quoted because & and ? are shell metacharacters.

instruction: From an array of records in data.json, print the id and name of each entry whose status is active, as raw text.
context: jq: -r emits strings without surrounding quotes. select keeps only values matching the predicate, and \(...) interpolates expressions inside a string literal.

instruction: Convert a pretty-printed JSON array into one compact JSON object per line.
context: jq: -c prints each result on a single line, which is exactly the JSON Lines format. Without -c jq pretty-prints, which breaks line-oriented tools downstream.

instruction: Count how many records a JSON Lines file contains.
context: jq: -s slurps the entire input stream into one array before filtering, which is how you aggregate across a JSON Lines file. Without -s the filter runs once per input value.

instruction: Count records by their status field in a JSON Lines file.
context: jq: group_by sorts and buckets by the key expression, producing an array of arrays. map then reduces each bucket, where .[0] samples the shared key and length gives the bucket size.

instruction: Make a script fail when a JSON response reports no results.
context: jq: -e sets the exit status from the last output value, returning 1 for false or null. Without -e jq exits zero as long as the filter itself ran, so the check silently passes.

instruction: Search only Rust files for the string 'unwrap' and show line numbers.
context: ripgrep: -t selects a predefined file type, and rg --type-list shows the mapping. Line numbers are on by default when output is a terminal. ripgrep also honors .gitignore automatically, unlike grep.

instruction: Search everything including hidden files and paths that gitignore would normally exclude.
context: ripgrep: -u reduces filtering in stages, so -uu disables both gitignore rules and hidden-file skipping, and -uuu additionally searches binary files. --hidden alone only re-enables dotfiles.

instruction: Search for a literal string that contains regex characters, such as a version constraint.
context: ripgrep: -F treats the pattern as a literal so dots, brackets, and plus signs lose their regex meaning. Without it, the dots would match any character and produce false positives.

instruction: Preview what a regex rename would look like without changing any files.
context: ripgrep: -r rewrites only the printed output and never edits files, so it is a safe preview. Capture groups are referenced as $1. Use sed -i or sd to actually apply the change.

instruction: Find panic calls in Rust sources with two lines of context, excluding the tests directory.
context: ripgrep: -C adds symmetric context lines, and repeated -g rules build an include/exclude set where a leading ! negates. Later globs take precedence over earlier ones.

instruction: Find every JSON file in the tree and check that each one parses.
context: fd: -e filters by extension without a leading dot, and -x runs a command per result with {} as the placeholder. -X instead batches all results into one invocation. jq empty parses and outputs nothing, failing on malformed input.

instruction: List directories named target anywhere in the tree, including ignored ones.
context: fd: -t d restricts results to directories, -H includes hidden entries, and -I disables gitignore filtering. Patterns are regular expressions by default, unlike find's glob-style -name.

instruction: Check whether the nginx service is running and see its recent output.
context: systemd: status shows the active state, the main PID, and the last few journal lines for the unit. is-active is the scriptable form because status uses a pager and returns non-zero for several distinct states.

instruction: Start a service immediately and make it start on boot.
context: systemd: enable creates the boot-time symlink but does not start the unit; --now performs both in one step. The mirror image is disable --now, which stops and unlinks.

instruction: List every systemd unit that is currently in a failed state.
context: systemd: --failed filters list-units to units in the failed state, which is the fastest post-boot triage. Add --user for the per-user manager, whose units are invisible to the system instance.

instruction: Make systemd pick up a unit file I just edited.
context: systemd: daemon-reload re-reads unit files from disk. Without it, systemctl restart keeps using the cached definition, which is why an edited unit appears to have no effect.

instruction: Show nginx log entries from the last fifteen minutes and keep following.
context: journald: -u filters by systemd unit, --since accepts absolute timestamps or relative English phrases, and -f follows new entries. -e instead jumps to the end without following.

instruction: Show only errors and worse from the current boot.
context: journald: -b limits output to the current boot and -b -1 selects the previous one. -p filters by syslog priority, where err is level 3 and includes everything more severe.

instruction: Find out how much disk space the systemd journal is consuming.
context: journald: --disk-usage reports the total size of all journal files. --vacuum-size=500M and --vacuum-time=7d prune them, which is the fix when /var/log has filled up.

instruction: See which installed Homebrew packages have updates available.
context: Homebrew: outdated lists installed formulae with newer versions, and --verbose shows the current and candidate versions side by side. brew update refreshes the formula index first and is a separate step.

instruction: Find out which installed packages depend on openssl before removing it.
context: Homebrew: uses lists formulae that depend on the named one, and --installed restricts that to what is actually present locally. Without --installed it searches the entire catalogue.

instruction: Run the build script for one workspace package and everything it depends on.
context: pnpm: --filter selects workspace packages, and the trailing ellipsis extends the selection to that package's dependencies. A leading ellipsis instead selects its dependents.

instruction: Install dependencies in CI so the build fails if the lockfile is stale.
context: pnpm: --frozen-lockfile refuses to modify pnpm-lock.yaml and errors when it disagrees with package.json. This is the default in CI environments and the guard against silent dependency drift.

instruction: List the models currently downloaded locally.
context: ollama: list shows locally pulled models with their size and digest. ollama ps shows which are loaded into memory right now, which is the one that matters for VRAM pressure. ollama ships no man page.
